assignedReviews.card_evidence: Paper was first made in ancient China!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies paper as an invention and its origin, but does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the invention's impact on everyday life as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Where was paper first made in the world?

Paper was first made in ancient China! It was the very first place in the world to create this amazing writing material.
copy.tl:
Saan unang ginawa ang papel sa buong mundo?

Ang papel ay unang ginawa sa sinaunang Tsina (China)! Ito ang kauna-unahang lugar sa buong mundo na lumikha ng kamanghangang panulat na ito.
copy.bis:
Asa unang gihimo ang papel sa tibuok kalibutan?

Ang papel unang gihimo sa karaang China (Tsina)! Mao kini ang una nga lugar sa tibuok kalibutan nga naghimo niining katingad-an nga panulat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood is full of tiny threads called cellulose fibers.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions tiny threads (cellulose fibers) in wood and paper, but does not describe the Particle Model of Matter (that all matter is made of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind). The fibers are not the fundamental particles of the model; the card is about material composition, not the particle model.

copy.en: Wood is full of tiny threads called cellulose fibers. These little threads are exactly what paper is made from!
copy.tl: Puno ng maninipis na hibla ang kahoy na tinatawag na cellulose fibers. Sila ang ginagamit para gumawa ng papel!
copy.bis: Puno sa nipis nga mga lanot ang kahoy nga gitawag og cellulose fibers. Sila ang gigamit sa paghimo og papel!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the wood is ground up into tiny pieces
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes grinding wood (a change in a solid material) but does not describe how the change makes the material useful, which is the core of G3-M-8. The card only explains the process of making pulp, not its usefulness or purpose.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it is mixed with water to make a soggy, mushy pulp
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows wood mixed with water to form a pulp, which is a mixture, but it does not classify the mixture as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it describe it as a solution or suspension. The competency requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures; this card does not address that classification.

copy.en:
How does wood turn into soggy pulp?

First, the wood is ground up into tiny pieces! Then, it is mixed with water to make a soggy, mushy pulp.
copy.tl:
Paano nagiging soggy pulp ang kahoy?

Una, dinudurog muna ang kahoy! Pagkatapos, hinaluan ito ng tubig para maging malabnaw at basang pulp.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa kahoy og soggy pulp?

Una, gigaling una ang kahoy! Dayon, gisagolan kini og tubig aron mahimong basa ug malabnaw nga pulp.

Paper was first made in China!
copy.tl:
Saan unang ginawa ang papel?

Ang papel ay unang ginawa sa Tsina (China)!
copy.bis:
Asa unang gihimo ang papel?

Ang papel unang gihimo sa China!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What illness comes from red-tide shellfish?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a harmful effect (paralytic shellfish poisoning) from red-tide shellfish, but it does not explain the interaction between living things or between living and non-living things that brings harm. It only names the illness and its symptoms, without describing the red tide phenomenon, the organisms involved, or the mechanism of harm. Thus it is related to the topic of harmful interactions but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
What illness comes from red-tide shellfish?

It's called paralytic shellfish poisoning, and it can cause numbness and weakness in the body.
copy.tl:
Anong sakit ang nakukuha sa kabibeng may red tide?

Tinatawag itong paralytic shellfish poisoning, at pwede itong magdulot ng pamamanhid at panghihina ng katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga sakit ang makuha sa kabibe nga adunay red tide?

Gitawag kini og paralytic shellfish poisoning, ug makahatag kini og pagkamanhod ug kaluya sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A parrot can live for 50 years or even more!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a parrot's lifespan. It does not compare life cycles or describe stages from egg to mature organism, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A parrot can live for 50 years or even more!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a living thing but does not describe growth, response, or reproduction. Lifespan alone is not a characteristic of living things as specified.

copy.en:
How long can a parrot live?

A parrot can live for 50 years or even more!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabuhay ang loro?

Ang loro ay maaaring mabuhay nang 50 taon o higit pa!
copy.bis:
Hangtod kanus-a mabuhi ang loro?

Ang loro makabuhi og 50 ka tuig o sobra pa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some parrots can copy human voices and the different sounds they hear around them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes vocal mimicry in parrots, which is not one of the listed characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not teach growth, response, or reproduction, so it is only related to the broad topic of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some parrots can copy human voices and the different sounds they hear around them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions copying sounds, which is a form of mimicry, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment or use secondary sources. It only states that parrots can copy sounds, without linking this to adaptation or environmental fit, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why can some parrots "talk"?

Some parrots can copy human voices and the different sounds they hear around them — that's why it sounds like talking.
copy.tl:
Bakit kayang "magsalita" ng ilang loro?

Kayang gayahin ng ilang loro ang tinig ng tao at iba't ibang tunog na naririnig nila kaya parang nagsasalita sila.
copy.bis:
Ngano makahimo og "sulti" ang ubang loro?

Ang ubang loro makahimo sa pagsundog sa tingog sa tawo ug sa lain-laing tunog nga ilang madungog, mao nga morag nagsulti sila.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that particles are arranged differently in the three states. It does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) nor use diagrams or flowcharts as required by G6-M-1.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the three states of matter but does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state, such as solid to liquid to gas. It provides no temperature-change content.

copy.en: Matter in solid, liquid, and gas states is made of particles, but the particles are arranged differently in each state.
copy.tl: Ang matter sa solid, liquid, at gas states ay gawa sa particles, pero magkakaiba ang pagkakaayos ng particles sa bawat state.
copy.bis: Ang matter sa solid, liquid, ug gas states gihimo sa particles, apan lahi ang pagkahan-ay sa particles sa matag state.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: milk or juice is heated just enough to kill harmful bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes pasteurization as a heat treatment to kill bacteria, which is a food-preservation example, but it does not address factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area) or any chemical reaction kinetics. The link to the competency is only through the broad topic of food preservation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: milk or juice is heated just enough to kill harmful bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heating a material (milk/juice) but does not describe changes in the properties of materials due to temperature, nor does it give an example like burning wood or coal. Pasteurization is about killing microbes, not about material property changes, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How is milk made safe to drink?

In pasteurization, milk or juice is heated just enough to kill harmful bacteria without ruining the taste!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawang ligtas ang gatas?

Sa pasteurization, iniinit nang sapat ang gatas o juice para mapatay ang nakakasamang bakterya nang di nasisira ang lasa!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimong luwas ang gatas?

Sa pasteurization, gipainit og igo ang gatas o juice aron mamatay ang makadaot nga bakterya nga dili madaot ang lami!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal covering its eggs, implying egg-laying, but does not identify the group (e.g., reptile) or contrast with live-bearing animals. It does not directly teach the classification of animals by reproductive method.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: to keep them warm and hidden from danger
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes keeping eggs warm and hidden, which relates to survival needs, but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. The warmth and protection are for eggs, not the animal's own basic needs.

copy.en: The pawikan covers its eggs with sand to keep them warm and hidden from danger.
copy.tl: Tinatabunan ng pawikan ng buhangin ang mga itlog nito para mapainit at maitago sa panganib.
copy.bis: Gitabonan sa pawikan og balas ang iyang mga itlog aron mainitan ug matago gikan sa peligro.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why does a sea turtle lay so many eggs?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a sea turtle (a reptile) laying eggs, but it does not teach the classification of animals into live-birth vs egg-laying groups, nor does it contrast mammals with birds/reptiles. The focus is on reproductive strategy (many eggs to compensate for losses), not on identifying which groups lay eggs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because only a few babies survive, so laying many eggs means enough still make it to keep the species going.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a reproductive strategy (laying many eggs because few survive) but does not describe an example of animals changing to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It is about survival of offspring, not adaptation through change.

copy.en:
Why does a sea turtle lay so many eggs?

Because only a few babies survive, so laying many eggs means enough still make it to keep the species going.
copy.tl:
Bakit maraming itlog ang inilalagay ng pawikan?

Dahil kakaunti lang ang makakaligtas, kailangan mangitlog nang marami para may sapat na matira para magpatuloy ang kanilang lahi.
copy.bis:
Nganong daghan ang itlog sa pawikan?

Kay pipila ra man ang maluwas, kinahanglan magbutang og daghang itlog aron igo ang mabilin aron magpadayon ang ilang banay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pawikan usually lays its eggs at night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a pawikan lays eggs at night. It does not identify pawikan as a reptile or place it in a group that reproduces by laying eggs, nor does it contrast egg-laying with live birth. This does not directly teach the competency's classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when the beach is safer and cooler
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a safer and cooler beach as a reason for night nesting, which is a behavioral adaptation, but it does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment over time, such as mimicry or camouflage. It lacks the evolutionary adaptation content required by the competency.

copy.en: The pawikan usually lays its eggs at night, when the beach is safer and cooler.
copy.tl: Karaniwang sa gabi nangingitlog ang pawikan dahil mas ligtas at malamig ang baybayin.
copy.bis: Kasagaran sa gabii mangitlog ang pawikan kay mas luwas ug bugnaw ang baybayon.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s

The card shares the theme of a famous Filipino and a product, but does not directly support the skill of identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en:
Who brought the yo-yo to the United States?

Pedro Flores! He was the Filipino who popularized the yo-yo in the US and opened the very first yo-yo factory there.
copy.tl:
Sino ang nagpasikat ng yo-yo sa Estados Unidos?

Si Pedro Flores! Siya ang Pilipinong nagpasikat ng yo-yo sa US at nagtayo ng unang pabrika ng yo-yo doon.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nagpabantog sa yo-yo sa Estados Unidos?

Si Pedro Flores! Siya ang Pilipino nga nagpabantog sa yo-yo sa US ug nagbukas sa unang pabrika sa yo-yo didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Intensity I (Scarcely Perceptible) is the weakest level!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the weakest intensity level but does not describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on magnitude. It mentions intensity, not magnitude, and gives no community-impact information. It is only tangentially related to earthquake effects.

copy.en:
What is Intensity I on the PEIS?

Intensity I (Scarcely Perceptible) is the weakest level! People barely feel it. You might only notice it through instruments or the slight wobble of water in a glass.
copy.tl:
Ano ang Intensity I sa PEIS?

Ang Intensity I (Scarcely Perceptible) ang pinakamahina! Halos hindi ito nararamdaman. Mapapansin mo lang ito sa mga instrumento o sa bahagyang pag-alon ng tubig sa baso.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang Intensity I sa PEIS?

Ang Intensity I (Scarcely Perceptible) mao ang pinakahuyang! Halos dili kini mabati. Mamatikdan lang nimo kini sa mga instrumento o sa gamayng paglihok sa tubig sa baso.

Is pencil 'lead' made of metal?

No! It is actually graphite mixed with clay.
copy.tl:
Gawa ba sa metal ang 'lead' ng lapis?

Hindi! Ito ay graphite na hinaluan ng luwad (clay).
copy.bis:
Gawa ba sa metal ang 'lead' sa lapis?

Dili! Kini graphite nga gisagolan og clay.

Why were pendulums used in old clocks?

Their steady, regular swing helps keep accurate time!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginagamit ang pendulum sa mga lumang orasan?

Ang tiyak at regular na ugoy nito ay tumutulong magsukat ng oras nang tama!
copy.bis:
Nganong gigamit ang pendulum sa daang mga orasan?

Ang tukma ug regular nga labyog niini makatabang sa pagsukod sa oras nga husto!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Galileo as a famous foreign scientist, but it does not identify any invention of his. The pendulum is a phenomenon he studied, not an invention. copy.en: It is said that Galileo studied the pendulum after watching a swinging lamp inside a church!
copy.tl: Sinasabing pinag-aralan ni Galileo ang pendulum pagkatapos niyang mapagmasdan ang isang umuugoy na lampara sa loob ng simbahan.
copy.bis: Giingon nga gitun-an ni Galileo ang pendulum human niyang makita ang naglabyog nga suga sulod sa simbahan.

copy.en:
What is the fixed point at the top of a pendulum called?

It is called the pivot! The pendulum hangs from it and swings all around this point.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa nakapirming punto sa itaas ng isang pendulum?

Tinatawag itong pivot! Nakabitin dito ang pendulum at umuugoy sa paligid ng puntong ito.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa pirmihang punto sa ibabaw sa usa ka pendulum?

Gitawag kini og pivot! Nagbitay ang pendulum dinhi ug naglabyog sa palibot niining punto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: swings back and forth when you let it go

assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a pendulum and describes its swinging motion, but does not mention gravity or explain how gravity affects the motion. It provides no direct instruction on observing or describing gravity's effects, only a related example of motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: swings back and forth when you let it go
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a pendulum swinging, which is a way an object moves, but it does not explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes or by people. copy.en:
What is a pendulum?

It's a weight hanging from a string or rod that swings back and forth when you let it go!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pendulum?

Ito ay isang bigat na nakabitin sa string o rod na umuugoy paroo't parito kapag binitawan!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pendulum?

Kini usa ka bug-at nga nagbitay sa pisi o sungkod nga magtabyog balik-balik kon buhian!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A playground swing and a music metronome both work exactly like a pendulum!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a swing, which involves pushes/pulls, but it does not demonstrate how pushes and pulls change speed or direction, nor does it involve guided activities. It is only a passing example of pendulum motion, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: A playground swing and a music metronome both work exactly like a pendulum!
copy.tl: Ang duyan sa palaruan at ang metronomo sa musika ay parehong gumagana na parang pendulum!
copy.bis: Ang duyan sa dulaanan ug ang metronomo sa musika parehong molihok sama sa pendulum!

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the emperor penguin's size but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, etc.). It only mentions a bird species, which is tangential to the classification competency.

copy.en:
Which penguin is the biggest of all?

The emperor penguin! It's the largest kind of penguin and can stand as tall as a young child.
copy.tl:
Alin ang pinakamalaking uri ng penguin?

Ang emperor penguin! Ito ang pinakamalaking uri ng penguin at maaaring umabot sa tangkad ng isang batang tao.
copy.bis:
Unsay pinakadako nga matang sa pingwino?

Ang emperor nga pingwino! Kini ang pinakadako nga matang sa pingwino ug makaabot sa gitas-on sa usa ka bata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all penguins live in ice and cold — some live in warmer places closer to the equator.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses penguin habitats in terms of temperature (cold vs. warm), not the terrestrial/aquatic/aerial classification of Philippine animals and plants required by G4-L-3. copy.en:
Do all penguins live in icy, cold places?

Not all penguins live in ice and cold — some live in warmer places closer to the equator.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng penguin ay nasa lamig at yelo lang?

Hindi lahat ng penguin ay nakatira sa lamig at yelo — may ilan na nasa mas maiinit na lugar malapit sa ekwador.
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga pingwino nagpuyo sa katugnaw ug yelo?

Dili tanang pingwino nagpuyo sa katugnaw ug yelo — ang uban naa sa mas init nga dapit duol sa ekwador.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can dive at more than 320 km/h (about 200 mph).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a speed value for a peregrine falcon's dive but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides no definition or relationship between distance and time, so it does not directly support the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en:
What is the fastest bird alive?

The peregrine falcon! It can dive at more than 320 km/h (about 200 mph).
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na ibon?

Ang peregrine falcon! Kayang sumisid nito nang mahigit 320 km/h (mga 200 mph).
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga langgam?

Ang peregrine falcon! Makasalom kini ug kapin sa 320 km/h (mga 200 mph).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are about 118 known elements!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the total number of known elements and their natural vs. laboratory origin. It does not identify the names or symbols of the first 20 or several common elements, which is the specific skill of G8-M-6. The content is related to the periodic table but provides no direct instructional support for naming or symbolizing elements.

copy.en:
How many elements are in the periodic table?

There are about 118 known elements! Around 90 are found naturally on Earth, and scientists made the rest in laboratories.
copy.tl:
Ilang elemento ang nasa periodic table?

May mga 118 na kilalang elemento! Mga 90 ay natural sa Daigdig, at ang iba ay ginawa ng mga scientist sa laboratoryo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that plastic and glass do not dissolve in water, but it does not identify the roles of solute and solvent in a solution, nor does it use the terms solute or solvent. It only touches on the concept of dissolving, which is related to solutions but does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: no matter how long you soak them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that soaking time does not cause plastic or glass to dissolve, which relates to factors affecting solubility. However, it does not demonstrate how factors such as heat affect solubility, nor does it investigate any factor systematically. It only states a single observation about insolubility, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Plastic and glass do not dissolve in water at all! They stay completely whole and unchanged, no matter how long you soak them.
copy.tl: Hindi natutunaw sa tubig ang plastik at salamin! Nananatili silang buo at walang pagbabago, gaano man katagal silang ibabad sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang plastik ug bildo dili matunaw sa tubig! Magpabilin silang buo ug walay pagbag-o, bisan unsa ka dugay sila ibabad sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just crumbles into super tiny pieces called microplastics. These hide in our water, soil, and even inside fish!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes plastic breaking into microplastics and their presence in water, soil, and fish, but it does not explain that this change is harmful to living or non-living things. The harm aspect central to G3-M-6 is not taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just crumbles into super tiny pieces called microplastics.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a physical breakdown of plastic but does not explain reversibility of physical changes or irreversibility of chemical changes. It does not address the physical vs chemical change distinction required by G6-M-3.

copy.en:
Does plastic really disappear when it breaks?

Nope! It just crumbles into super tiny pieces called microplastics. These hide in our water, soil, and even inside fish!
copy.tl:
Nawawala ba talaga ang plastik kapag nabasag?

Hindi! Nagiging napakaliliit na piraso lang itong tinatawag na microplastics. Nakatago ito sa tubig, lupa, at kahit sa loob ng isda!
copy.bis:
Mawala ba gyud ang plastik kung mabuak?

Dili! Mahimo lang kining gagmay kaayo nga piraso nga gitawag og microplastics. Nagtago kini sa tubig, yuta, ug bisan sa sulod sa isda!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The energy moving the plates comes from Earth's internal heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to describe and explain what mechanisms that drive the movement of tectonic plates including the role of the asthenosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the internal heat source (leftover heat and radioactive decay) that ultimately drives plate motion, which is background for understanding the mechanisms. However, it does not describe or explain the actual mechanisms (e.g., convection currents) nor the role of the asthenosphere, which are the core of the competency.

copy.en: The energy moving the plates comes from Earth's internal heat! It is partly leftover heat from when the planet formed, and partly from decaying radioactive materials.
copy.tl: Ang enerhiyang nagpapagalaw sa mga plato ay galing sa init ng Earth! Bahagi nito ay natitirang init mula sa pagkakabuo ng planeta, at bahagi mula sa pagkabulok ng radioactive materials.
copy.bis: Ang enerhiya nga nagpalihok sa mga plato gikan sa kainit sa Earth! Usa ka bahin niini nahibilin nga kainit gikan sa pagporma sa planeta, ug bahin gikan sa pagkadunot sa radioactive materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A plateau is a wide landform that is flat on top but raised higher than the land around it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a plateau as a landform, which is background knowledge for identifying local landforms, but it does not provide local examples or describe how landforms influence living and non-living components, which are the core actions of the competency.

copy.en:
What is a plateau?

A plateau is a wide landform that is flat on top but raised higher than the land around it!
copy.tl:
Ano ang plateau?

Ang plateau o talampas ay malawak na anyong lupa na patag ang ibabaw pero mas mataas kaysa sa nakapaligid na lupa!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang plateau?

Ang plateau o talampas usa ka lapad nga porma sa yuta nga patag ang ibabaw apan mas habog kaysa sa yuta nga naglibot niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It converts harmful exhaust gases like carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into less harmful carbon dioxide and nitrogen.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a catalytic conversion of exhaust gases and its environmental benefit, but it does not address the specific reaction types named in the competency (combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, respiration) nor explain how those important types of chemical reactions impact the natural and built environments. It shares the broad theme of chemical reactions affecting the environment but provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Platinum is used as a catalyst in car catalytic converters! It converts harmful exhaust gases like carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into less harmful carbon dioxide and nitrogen.
copy.tl: Ang platinum ay ginagamit bilang catalyst sa catalytic converter ng mga sasakyan! Binibago nito ang mapanganib na carbon monoxide at nitrogen oxides sa mas hindi mapanganib na carbon dioxide at nitrogen.
copy.bis: Ang platinum gigamit isip catalyst sa catalytic converter sa mga sasakyan! Nagconvert kini sa mga delikadong exhaust gas sama sa carbon monoxide ug nitrogen oxides ngadto sa mas dili delikadong carbon dioxide ug nitrogen.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A gland in the thigh of the male platypus makes the venom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an internal venom gland and its connection to a spur, not the outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement or food gathering. It shares the topic of animal body parts but does not directly support the competency's skill of observing/describing outer parts for locomotion or feeding.

copy.en:
Where does a platypus's venom come from?

A gland in the thigh of the male platypus makes the venom, and it connects to the spur through a tube.
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang kamandag ng platypus?

May glandula sa hita ng lalaking platypus na gumagawa ng kamandag, at ito ay nakakabit sa tibo nito sa pamamagitan ng isang daluyan.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang hilo sa platypus?

Adunay glandula sa paa sa laki nga platypus nga naghimo sa hilo, ug kini konektado sa tibo pinaagi sa usa ka tubo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It causes intense pain and swelling that can last for days or even weeks!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a platypus spur (a body part) but does not describe outer body parts or their role in movement and food gathering. The content is about the venom's effect (pain and swelling), not about the structure or function of body parts for locomotion or feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It causes intense pain and swelling that can last for days or even weeks!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the effect of a platypus spur (venom causing pain and swelling) but does not describe how an animal has changed to better suit its environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. The spur's venom is a defensive adaptation, but the card does not explain it as an environmental adaptation or use secondary sources to describe such changes.

copy.en:
What happens if a platypus spur stabs you?

It causes intense pain and swelling that can last for days or even weeks!
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kapag natusok ka ng tibo ng platypus?

Nagdudulot ito ng matinding kirot at pamamaga na maaaring tumagal ng ilang araw hanggang linggo!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung matuhog ka sa tibo sa platypus?

Maghatag kini og grabe nga sakit ug hubag nga mahimong molungtad og pipila ka adlaw hangtod semana!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pluto was discovered in the year 1930!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the year Pluto was discovered. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition, which is what G5-E-11 requires. The fact is merely related to the solar system topic.

copy.en:
Do you know when Pluto was discovered?

Pluto was discovered in the year 1930! That is the exact year it was found.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba kung kailan natuklasan ang Pluto?

Natuklasan ang Pluto noong 1930! Iyan ang eksaktong taon nang ito makita.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka kung kanus-a nadiskobre ang Pluto?

Nadiskobre ang Pluto niadtong 1930! Mao na ang eksaktong tuig sa kini nakit-an.
